headline: Strait of Hormuz Crisis Drives WTI Above $100 as Canada Posts 0.1% GDP Growth and 84,000 Job Losses

key_indicators.label: BOC RATE
key_indicators.change: Held (7th consecutive meeting at this level after 7 cuts from 5.00%)

facts.statement: The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since approximately March 2, disrupting approximately 20 million barrels per day of oil flows (~20% of global seaborne oil trade). WTI crude settled at $102.88/bbl on March 30 — the first settlement above $100 since July 2022. Brent surged approximately 55% in March to $112.78/bbl, a record monthly gain for the contract since inception in 1988.
facts.source_title: CNBC — Brent Record Monthly Surge, WTI Above $100
connections: The database tracks 63 oil_gas projects and 785 power_energy projects across Canada
Dallas Fed estimated a one-quarter closure could raise WTI to $98/bbl average and reduce global GDP growth by an annualized 2.9 percentage points in Q2 2026
Alberta has 727 tracked projects that include upstream oil and gas operations

facts.statement: Statistics Canada reported employment declined by 84,000 (-0.4%) in February 2026, reversing Q4 2025 gains. Full-time employment fell 108,000; private-sector employment dropped 73,000. The unemployment rate rose to 6.7%, up 0.2 percentage points from January. Participation rate declined 0.1pp to 64.9%.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Labour Force Survey, February 2026
connections: Services-producing industries lost 56,000 jobs (-0.3%); goods-producing industries lost 28,000 (-0.7%)
The database tracks 1,034 projects currently under construction that depend on labour market conditions
Wholesale and retail trade lost 18,000 jobs — the largest subsector decline

facts.statement: Real GDP rose 0.1% in January 2026, marking a second consecutive monthly increase. Mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction expanded 1.2%. Manufacturing contracted 1.4%. Advance estimate indicates 0.2% growth in February. Q4 2025 GDP contracted 0.2% annualized.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — GDP by Industry, January 2026
connections: Manufacturing contraction (-1.4%) affects 49 tracked manufacturing projects
Mining/oil/gas expansion (+1.2%) affects 364 mining and 63 oil_gas projects in the database
Full-year 2025 GDP growth was approximately 1.7%; IMF projects 1.6% for 2026

facts.statement: Headline CPI fell to 1.8% year-over-year in February 2026, down from 2.3% in January — the lowest reading since early 2021. Core measures converged: CPI-median at 2.3%, CPI-trim at 2.3%, CPI-common at 2.4%. Food inflation slowed to 5.3% from 7.3% in January.
connections: CPI below the 2% target supports the BoC's decision to hold at 2.25%
The March CPI release is scheduled for April 15 — same day as the next BoC rate decision with full MPR
211 residential projects tracked in the database are sensitive to rate and inflation dynamics

facts.statement: The Bank of Canada held its overnight rate at 2.25% on March 18, citing weaker near-term growth from US tariffs. The Governing Council stated it would 'proceed carefully' given heightened uncertainty. Bond markets price ~86% probability of no change at the April 15 meeting.
facts.source_title: Bank of Canada — March 18 Rate Decision
connections: Seven consecutive cuts from June 2024 peak of 5.00% brought the rate to current 2.25%
Next rate decision: April 15, 2026 with full Monetary Policy Report
Variable mortgage rates have declined in line with BoC cuts; fixed rates held firm due to elevated long-term bond yields

facts.statement: Canada's merchandise trade deficit widened to $3.6 billion in January 2026, from $1.3 billion in December 2025. Motor vehicle and parts exports dropped 21.2% to $5.4 billion — the lowest since September 2021. Energy product exports partially offset, rising 4.1%.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — International Merchandise Trade, January 2026
connections: US tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum exports remain in effect
Motor vehicle exports at lowest since Sep 2021 — affects 49 manufacturing projects and 600 transport_logistics projects
February trade data release scheduled for April 2 — first full month following Strait of Hormuz closure

bocRate.context: The Bank of Canada held steady at 2.25% for the seventh consecutive meeting at this level, following seven cuts from the June 2024 peak of 5.00%. The Governing Council cited weaker near-term growth from US tariffs.

realGdp.context: Real GDP rose 0.1% in January 2026, a second consecutive monthly gain. Goods-producing industries expanded 0.2%; services were essentially unchanged. Advance estimate for February is +0.2%.

tradeBalance.context: Trade deficit widened to $3.6B from $1.3B. Exports fell 4.7% to $62.5B; imports declined 1.1% to $66.1B. Motor vehicle exports dropped 21.2%.

retailSales.context: Retail sales rose 1.1% to $70.7B. Core retail (ex gasoline and motor vehicles) up 0.9%. Motor vehicle dealers led gains (+2.0%). Advance estimate for February: +0.9%.

indicatorContextLines.bocRate: The Bank of Canada held steady at 2.25% on March 18, following seven consecutive cuts from the June 2024 peak of 5.00%, citing weaker near-term growth from US tariffs and stating it would 'proceed carefully' given heightened uncertainty.
indicatorContextLines.realGdp: Real GDP rose 0.1% in January 2026, a second consecutive monthly increase. Mining, quarrying, and oil/gas extraction expanded 1.2%; manufacturing contracted 1.4%. Advance information indicates 0.2% growth in February.
indicatorContextLines.cpi: Headline CPI fell to 1.8% YoY in February 2026 from 2.3% in January, the lowest since early 2021. All three core measures (median 2.3%, trim 2.3%, common 2.4%) are converging toward the BoC's 2% target.
indicatorContextLines.unemployment: The unemployment rate rose to 6.7% in February, up 0.2pp from January, as employment declined 84,000. Full-time employment fell 108,000 and private-sector employment dropped 73,000.
indicatorContextLines.housingStarts: Housing starts ran at 250,900 SAAR in February 2026, up 4.5% from 240,148 in January. The six-month trend declined 0.4% to 256,005 units. CMHC noted the trend remains 'relatively steady' despite monthly volatility.
indicatorContextLines.tradeBalance: The merchandise trade deficit widened to $3.6B in January from $1.3B in December. Motor vehicle and parts exports dropped 21.2% to $5.4B, the lowest since September 2021. Energy exports partially offset, rising 4.1%.

indicatorContextLines.consumerConfidence: Consumer confidence declined to 47.50 in February from 49.30 in January. The Bloomberg/Nanos index showed a three-week slide into late March. However, the proportion of Canadians expecting the economy to strengthen in six months rose from 17% to 26%.

cross_references.interpretation: WTI surpassing $100/bbl for the first time since July 2022 driven by Strait of Hormuz closure. The database tracks 63 oil_gas projects and 727 projects in Alberta.

Manufacturing contraction due to weakness in durable and non-durable goods. Motor vehicle exports dropped 21.2%. US tariffs on steel and aluminum remain in effect. The database tracks 49 manufacturing projects.
Employment decline was broad-based: services lost 56,000 and goods lost 28,000. 1,034 projects under construction depend on labour market conditions.
Housing starts rose despite labour market weakness. The $8.8B federal-Ontario housing deal targets 800,000+ potential housing starts. The database tracks 211 residential projects.
Gold declined from a peak of $5,161/oz on March 3 to $4,578 by month-end, driven by margin liquidation and USD strength. The database tracks 364 mining projects.

key_developments: Federal Reserve held federal funds rate at 3.50-3.75% at March 18 meeting, following three 25bps cuts in late 2025, citing 'heightened uncertainty' from geopolitical risk and volatile energy prices
Equity markets in March dominated by Strait of Hormuz crisis — S&P 500 at ~6,496 on March 31, down approximately 9.4% from its January 2026 peak
US tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum exports remain in effect; BoC attributes weaker Canadian near-term growth partly to these trade disruptions
Reports of potential US-Iran diplomatic talks on March 31 triggered a broad equity market rally (S&P +2.40%, Nasdaq +3.24%)
global_package.canada_impact: US rate hold at 3.50-3.75% exceeds Canada's 2.25%, maintaining a 125-150bp spread that puts downward pressure on the Canadian dollar (CAD/USD 0.7198, -1.85% M/M). US tariffs on steel and aluminum directly affect Canadian manufacturing exports; motor vehicle exports dropped 21.2% to $5.4B in January. Strait of Hormuz crisis elevates energy export revenues but introduces supply chain cost pressures.

key_developments: ECB held deposit facility rate at 2.00% at March 19 meeting
Euro area HICP inflation at 1.9% YoY in Q4 2025 — below ECB's 2% target
GDP grew 0.2% Q/Q in Q4 2025; Germany recorded a second consecutive annual GDP contraction
EUR/USD at approximately 1.1460 on March 31 — euro strengthened against USD amid geopolitical uncertainty
global_package.canada_impact: ECB rate at 2.00% vs BoC at 2.25% creates a narrow differential. Germany's continued contraction reduces demand for Canadian resource exports to Europe. CETA (Canada-EU trade agreement) trade flows affected by eurozone weakness. Euro strength against USD indirectly affects CAD competitiveness in European markets.

key_developments: Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% at March 18 meeting (unanimous vote)
UK CPI at 2.8% in February 2026 — above BoE 2% target
GDP grew 0.1% Q/Q in Q4 2025; weak growth trajectory continues
global_package.canada_impact: UK-Canada trade under CPTPP framework. BoE rate at 3.75% — 150bp above BoC — reflects persistent UK inflation. GBP movements affect pricing for Canadian resource and agri-food exports to the UK. Weak UK growth limits expansion of bilateral trade volumes.

key_developments: Manufacturing PMI rose to 50.4 in March 2026, above the 50.0 expansion threshold after two months of contraction (49.3 in Jan, 49.0 in Feb)
Non-manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 from 49.5; new export orders showed strength
Higher shipping costs and imported commodity costs from the Middle East conflict weighed on input prices
global_package.canada_impact: China is Canada's second-largest merchandise trading partner (~5% of exports). Manufacturing PMI returning to expansion after two months of contraction could increase demand for Canadian crude oil, canola, potash, wood products, and seafood. Strait of Hormuz crisis raises shipping costs for Canadian LNG and commodity exports routed to Asia. China controls ~60% of global rare earth mine production, affecting Canadian critical minerals projects.

globalVectors.us: The Federal Reserve held at 3.50-3.75% on March 18, maintaining a 125-150bp spread above the BoC's 2.25%. US tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum remain in effect, contributing to a 21.2% drop in motor vehicle exports. Potential US-Iran diplomatic talks reported March 31 triggered equity rallies.
globalVectors.china: China's manufacturing PMI returned to expansion at 50.4 in March after two months of contraction. Higher shipping costs from the Strait of Hormuz closure weigh on input prices. Canada-China commodity trade flows in crude oil, canola, potash, and wood products remain active under the current bilateral framework.
globalVectors.eu: The ECB held at 2.00% with HICP at 1.9%. Germany recorded a second consecutive annual GDP contraction. CETA trade flows with Canada are subject to eurozone demand conditions. The euro strengthened to 1.1460 against the USD.
globalVectors.uk: The BoE held at 3.75% unanimously with CPI at 2.8%. UK GDP grew 0.1% Q/Q in Q4 2025. UK-Canada trade operates under the CPTPP framework; weak UK growth limits bilateral trade expansion.

watchlist_package.description: Detailed account of the Governing Council's March 18 rate decision deliberations, including assessment of US tariff impacts and inflation outlook.
Monthly export and import data. February is the first full month following the Strait of Hormuz closure initiation. Watch for shifts in energy and automotive trade volumes.
First Q2 labour market reading. February showed -84,000 employment change; March data will indicate whether the decline continued or reversed.
Monthly permit values by province and sector; leading indicator for residential and non-residential construction pipeline. 1,671 infrastructure projects tracked in the database.
Monthly CPI release. March is the final month affected by the GST/HST base-year effect. February headline CPI was 1.8%. Releases same day as BoC rate decision.

watchlist_package.event_name: Policy Interest Rate Announcement + Monetary Policy Report
watchlist_package.description: Rate decision with full MPR. Bond markets price ~86% probability of hold at 2.25%, ~14% probability of 25bps hike. Most data-dense event in the near-term calendar.
Monthly retail sales by province. January retail was $70.7B (+1.1%); advance estimate for February is +0.9%.
Monthly real GDP output by industry. January GDP was +0.1%; advance for February is +0.2%. Covers manufacturing, construction, and resource extraction.
Parliamentary review of Budget 2026 implementation legislation. Infrastructure funding, housing accelerator, and defence provisions are in scope.
April employment data; first Q2 labour market reading following federal budget measures. Provincial breakdowns across all 13 provinces.
Second monthly CPI reading of Q2. Monitors pass-through of tariff-related and energy cost pressures on goods categories. First post-base-effect CPI reading.
March permit values complete the Q1 construction intentions picture for residential and non-residential sectors.
Completes the Q1 2026 monthly GDP sequence. Final input before the Q1 expenditure-based GDP release.
June rate decision. BoC will have full Q1 GDP, two Q2 CPI prints, and Q1 LFS data available for this deliberation.
May employment data with provincial breakdowns covering all 13 provinces.
Third monthly CPI reading of Q2. Cumulative read on whether tariff and energy price effects are persisting.
First monthly GDP reading for Q2 2026; early signal on whether economic momentum carried through the budget period.
July rate decision with updated Monetary Policy Report. Mid-year assessment of inflation trajectory and growth conditions.
September rate decision. BoC will have Q2 GDP expenditure accounts and two summer CPI prints available.
October rate decision with full Monetary Policy Report update. Q3 GDP data and CPI trajectory inform this deliberation.
Final BoC rate decision of 2026. Sets the policy rate heading into year-end and provides forward guidance for 2027.

infographic_directives.title: Strait of Hormuz Impact: March Commodity Price Moves
infographic_directives.subtitle: WTI +50%, Brent +55%, Gold -14%, Uranium -17%, Steel -10.4%
infographic_directives.insight: The Strait of Hormuz closure since March 2 drove the largest crude oil monthly gains since 2008 — WTI to $102.88/bbl, Brent to $112.78/bbl. Gold fell 14% from margin liquidation. Steel and uranium proxies also declined 10-17% month-over-month.

infographic_directives.title: BoC Rate vs. Canadian Dollar (12-Month Trend)
infographic_directives.subtitle: Policy rate at 2.25% while CAD/USD weakened to 0.7198 (-1.85% M/M)
infographic_directives.insight: The BoC has held at 2.25% since cutting seven times from 5.00%. The US-Canada rate spread of 125-150bp continues to put downward pressure on the loonie, which weakened past 1.38 per USD to a two-month low in March.

infographic_directives.title: January GDP by Major Sector: Goods vs. Services Split
infographic_directives.subtitle: Mining/O&G +1.2%, Retail +0.8%, Manufacturing -1.4%
infographic_directives.insight: Goods-producing industries expanded 0.2% for the second straight month in January, driven by mining (+1.2%) and construction. Manufacturing contracted 1.4%. Services were essentially unchanged — retail (+0.8%) and finance offset declines in wholesale and transportation.

infographic_directives.title: Project Database by Status (7,372 Total Projects)
infographic_directives.subtitle: Under Review 2,591 | Proposed 2,528 | Under Construction 1,034 | Approved 549
infographic_directives.insight: The database tracks 7,372 capital projects across Canada. 2,591 are under review, 2,528 proposed, 1,034 under construction, 549 approved, 486 complete, 153 cancelled, and 31 on hold. Infrastructure (1,671), power/energy (785), and transport/logistics (600) are the three largest sector categories.
